## Part 2 — Interpretation

### Background

Parent #533's bare-word install-step grid found that a bare `pirate`/`villain` role header carries LESS wrong-persona marker mass than a content-matched minimal system prompt from install onward — but its apparent average-leakage advantage hid a probe split, and the comparison lived partly in a saturated regime where cross-arm log-p contrasts reduce to base-prior differences. This task re-read the parent's committed four-float logit captures with two cleaner measuring sticks: (a) the unsaturated checkpoints (s18 is the only point where both arms sit in/adjacent to the [5, 12]-nat usable band, at matched log-p implant strength, before any emission), and (b) the EOS-margin readout Δ(z_marker − z_eos), which is gauge-invariant and cannot be compressed by the softmax ceiling (valid here because LoRA excludes the unembedding — `gauge_assert.ok` on all 240 cells). Zero new training; the manipulated variable is the readout/regime. The plan's preview (computed during planning over these same files) pointed at the confirmed outcome; the production run re-derived everything from raw arrays with the verdict logic frozen in the plan — this is **disclosed preview-confirmation on the same draws**, not an independent replication.

### Headline (operational narration, per the registered classifier)

**The role header leaks less at the wrong-persona probe but more at the default-assistant probe, under both clean reads.** The frozen classifier returns `concentration_confirmed` — "concentration" is this task's registered operational name for that two-probe pattern, mirroring the Goal; it is **not a mechanism claim**. Scope sentence (binding): the measured 2-probe split does not adjudicate between redistribution/conservation of leakage mass, format-proximity of the default-assistant context to the role-header encoding, or differential effectiveness of the contrastive negatives across arms.

### Finding 1 — The default-assistant excess is unconditional in this grid, and it is the base-prior-clean half

At the default-assistant probe — the only probe whose encoding is identical across arms, so the base prior is identical (−22.09, atol 1e-4) and the cross-arm contrast is base-prior-clean — the role arm carries MORE marker mass at EVERY checkpoint, on BOTH personas, in BOTH spaces: 16 of 16 cells CI-clear in the role-leaks-more direction, with 0/5 positive seeds in 15 cells (1/5 in pirate s120 margin). Villain, where the arms' own-slot implant strengths are matched throughout (within ~1.1 nat in margin space at s≤60), holds a stable excess of ~1.3-1.6 nats at all four checkpoints. This half survives the in-band read (s18, both arms pre-emission), the install-onset read (s30), and the ceiling-free margin read — the parent's average-leakage framing had partially hidden it because the pirate log-p contrast collapses to −0.27 nat at s120 where the margin still reads −1.79 [−2.66, −0.70].

### Finding 2 — The wrong-persona advantage is real from install onward, but absent (and on villain slightly reversed) at the in-band pre-emission point

In margin space at install-onward checkpoints the role arm's wrong-persona advantage is CI-clear on both personas at all of {30, 60, 120}, 5/5 seeds everywhere, growing from ~+0.5 at s30 to ~+3.1 nats (villain s60). But at s18 — the only checkpoint inside the usable band, where own argmax-emit is 0.000 on every arm (in-band but **pre-emission-gate**, NOT "installed off-saturation") — the advantage is ABSENT in log-p space (pirate −0.24 [−0.58, +0.11]; villain −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15]). The classifier's off-saturation verdict is "shrinks": install-coupled, absent at the in-band sub-install point. The advantage is created between s18 and s30, by the install dynamics, not present in the pre-install encoding geometry.

### Finding 3 — The villain s18 margin reversal (a finding in its own right)

At s18 in margin space, villain's wrong-persona contrast is CI-clear in the OPPOSITE direction: d = −0.231 [−0.377, −0.077], 1/5 seeds positive — the minimal SYSTEM prompt leaks slightly less than the role header before the emission gate. The magnitude is small (~0.2 nat against the +0.5 to +3.1 install-onward advantages), but it is not noise by the registered criterion, and it sharpens Finding 2: on villain the pre-install geometry tilts mildly against the role header, and the role advantage that emerges at s30+ is entirely an install-dynamics product. (Log-p space at the same cell straddles: −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15].)

### Finding 4 — Pirate's default slot crosses the emission threshold; the role arm gets there harder (the deployment-relevant number)

The three saturation-flagged cells (pirate-default s30/s60/s120) are exactly where the role-arm pirate model's default-assistant slot approaches the argmax ceiling. At these argmax-adjacent cells — and only here, per the registered scope rule — the excess can be stated in emission terms: at s60/s120 the role-arm pirate model's mean log P(marker) at the default-assistant slot reaches −0.41 / −0.28 (mean per-question probability gain 0.89 / 0.92), i.e. the marker holds the majority of next-token probability at the fixed post-response slot under the bare default-assistant context, vs −1.32 / −0.55 (0.64 / 0.84) for the system arm. Both arms cross the greedy-emission threshold at the default context by s120 on pirate; the role arm crosses earlier and harder. Caveat: this is teacher-forced after BASE-model greedy responses — on-policy default-context responses from the trained model could shift the slot — so it is emission onset at the fixed probe slot, not measured behavioral emission frequency. Everywhere else in the grid, default-slot excess is leakage MASS at a probe slot, not behavior (wrong-persona behavioral emission is 0 across all 4,000 probes of this grid).

### Finding 5 — Honesty check on implant-strength matching (own-slot margin gauge)

The round-1 critique added own-slot Δmargin so cross-arm strength matching could be checked past the log-p ceiling. It shows: villain arms matched throughout (≤1.1 nat apart at s≤60); pirate arms matched in log-p space at s18 (12.12 vs 12.60) but NOT in margin space (12.82 vs 16.74 — role ~3.9 nat latently stronger), with the gap persisting at s30 (25.8 vs 31.4) and INVERTING at s120 (41.1 vs 38.4 — system stronger). Implication: part of the pirate default-half magnitude at s18-s60 may track the role arm's stronger latent implant rather than the encoding per se. Two observations keep the half intact: (i) villain is strength-matched and shows the reversal CI-clear at every checkpoint; (ii) at s120 the reversal holds on both personas while the latent strength gradient points the OTHER way (system stronger). Symmetrically for the wrong half: the s60 advantage runs AGAINST the strength gradient (role latently stronger yet leaks less — the cleanest install-onward read), while the pirate s120 advantage (+1.83) is smaller than system's latent own-slot excess (+2.7) and so is not individually separable from strength there. Magnitudes should be read with this in mind; the directional verdicts do not depend on it.

1. The bare role header's "containment advantage" from #533 is probe-specific: real (and growing with training) at the wrong-persona probe from install onward, but inverted at the default-assistant probe at every checkpoint — and the default-assistant context is the safety-relevant one (leakage-to-default, open-q 3.7).
